rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people destined for Hell are disbelieving jinn and humans who turn away from contemplating God’s signs.
rows.anchor: هم الكفار من الفريقين المعرضون عن تدبر آيات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knew their chosen disbelief eternally, willed and created it in them, and made Hell their destination accordingly.
rows.anchor: والله تعالى علم منهم اختيار الكفر فشاء منهم الكفر وخلق فيهم ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This does not conflict with 51:56: those eternally known to worship were created for worship, while those known to disbelieve were created for what God knew they would do; a general wording can intend a specific group.
rows.anchor: فالحاصل أن من علم منه فى الأزل أنه يكون منه العبادة خلقه للعبادة

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites take the lām as indicating outcome, saying Hell was their end; al-Nasafī rejects this as departing from the apparent wording to avoid attributing sins to God’s will.
rows.anchor: وقول المعتزلة بأن هذه لام العاقبة أى لما كان عاقبتهم جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hearts do not grasp truth, their eyes do not see right guidance, and their ears do not hear admonition.
rows.anchor: ﴾ الحق ولا يتفكرون فيه ﴿ ولهم أعين لا يبصرون بها ﴾ الرشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They resemble cattle in failing to understand, observe for reflection, or listen thoughtfully.
rows.anchor: فى عدم الفقه والنظر للاعتبار والاستماع للتفكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are more astray because they defy reason, oppose the messenger, and commit depravity, while cattle pursue benefit and avoid harm; accountable humans choose what harms them.
rows.anchor: لأنهم كابروا العقول وعاندوا الرسول وارتكبوا الفضلو فالأنعام تطلب منافعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A human combines spirit and appetite, heaven and earth: spirit mastering desire surpasses the angels, while desire mastering spirit surpasses earthly beasts.
rows.anchor: فالآدمى روحانى شهوانى سماوى ارضى فإن غلب روحه هواه فاق ملائكة السموات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are the fully consummate heedless ones.
rows.anchor: الكاملون فى الغفلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s names are most beautiful because they indicate beautiful meanings: some belong to His reality, some are valued for their effects, and some invite emulation.
rows.anchor: التى هى أحسن الأسماء لانها تدل على معان حسنة فمنها ما يستحقه بحقائقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The names grounded in divine reality include the Eternal, Everlasting, All-Powerful, All-Knowing, and the One unlike anything.
rows.anchor: كالقديم قيل كل شيء والباقى بعد كل شيء والقادر على كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Names appreciated for their effects include Forgiving, Merciful, Appreciative, and Forbearing; other names call for adopting qualities such as generosity.
rows.anchor: ومنها ما تستحسنه الانفس لآثارها كالغفور والرحيم والشكور والحليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Call God by these names and leave those who depart from their truth by assigning Him unscripted names or descriptions such as body, substance, intellect, or cause.
rows.anchor: واتركوا تسمية الذين يميلون عن الحق والصواب فيها فيسمونه بغير الأسماء الحسنى

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamzah reads the verb for deviating from God’s names with the form yalḥadūn, from laḥada, to turn aside.
rows.anchor: يلحدون حمزة لحد الحد مال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial comparison is nominative: these people’s way is like the way of Pharaoh’s people.
rows.anchor: فى محل الرفع أى دأب هؤلاء مثل دأب آل فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dāʾb means the habitual practice and work in which people persist.
rows.anchor: ودأبهم عادتهم وعملهم الذى دأبوا فيه أى داوموا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who came before may mean those before Quraysh or those before Pharaoh’s people.
rows.anchor: من قبل قريش أو قبل آل فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelief explains the earlier people’s habitual course: they persisted in denial, so God punished them as He had punished their predecessors.
rows.anchor: جروا على عادتهم في التكذيب فأجرى عليهم مثل ما فعل بهم في التعذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative refers either to the punishment or to the retribution.
rows.anchor: العذاب أو الانتقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s wisdom does not change a people’s blessing until they change their own condition; a worsened state then gives way to still harsher consequences.
rows.anchor: بسبب أن الله لم يصح فى حكمته أن يغير نعمته عند قوم حتى يغيروا ما بهم من الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s people and Meccan polytheists were unbelievers before the messenger came; after rejecting his signs and seeking his death, they lost their respite and were hastened into punishment.
rows.anchor: فلما بعث اليهم بالآيات فكذبوه وسعوا فى إراقة دمه غيروا حالهم إلى أسوأ مما كانت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears what the deniers of messengers say and knows what they do.
rows.anchor: ﴾ لما يقول مكذبوا الرسل ﴿ عليم ﴾ بما يفعلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger is Muhammad, of the people’s human kind and their Arab Quraysh lineage.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لقد جاءكم رسول ﴾ محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hardship pains him because he is one of them, and he fears that they will fall into punishment.
rows.anchor: شديد عليه شاق لكونه بعضا منكم عنتكم ولقاءكم المكروه فهو يخاف عليكم الوقوع فى العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is eager for their faith.
rows.anchor: ﴿ حريص عليكم ﴾ على ايمانكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His tenderness and mercy extend to believers from among the addressees and from elsewhere.
rows.anchor: ﴿ بالمؤمنين ﴾ منكم ومن غيركم ﴿ رؤوف رحيم ﴾

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported view says God has combined two of His names for no one else besides the Messenger of God.
rows.anchor: قيل لم يجمع الله اسمين من أسمائه لأحد غير رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their supplication is their address to God, O God, we glorify You; they delight in remembering Him, not merely worshipping.
rows.anchor: أى دعاؤهم لأن اللهم نداء لله ومعناه اللهم أنا نسبحك أى يدعون الله بقولهم سبحانك اللهم تلذذا بذكره لاعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that the people greet one another with peace.
rows.anchor: أى يحيى بعضهم بعضا بالسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the angels greet them with peace; the source describes the construction as a verbal noun attached to its object.
rows.anchor: أو هى تحية الملائكة إياهم واضيف المصدر إلى المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation is that God Himself greets them.
rows.anchor: أو تحية الله لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final supplication is the conclusion of their glorification, namely their saying that praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وآخر دعواهم ﴾ وخاتمة دعائهم الذى هو التسبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle an is the lightened form of anna; its original construction includes the pronoun of the affair.
rows.anchor: أن مخففة من الثقيلة واصله أنه الحمد لله رب العالمين والضمير للشأن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported view says they begin with glorification and end in praise, exalting God first and giving thanks last while speaking as they wish between them.
rows.anchor: قيل أول كلامهم التسبيح و آخره التحميد فيبتدءون بتعظيم الله وتنزيهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥattā begins a new conditional clause and marks the endpoint of Noah’s ark-building; the intervening material describes the circumstances while he built it.
rows.anchor: هى التى يبتدا بعدها الكلام أدخلت على الجملة من الشرط والجزاء وهى غاية لقوله ويصنع الفلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whenever a group of Noah’s people passed him, they mocked him; the clause can be the answer to kullamā, an apposition to passed, or an adjective of the group.
rows.anchor: كلما مر عليه ملأ من قومه سخروا منه وجواب كلما سخروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase saying that Noah spoke may resume after an implied question, or it may answer the conditional clause.
rows.anchor: وقال استئناف على تقدير سؤال سائل أو قال جواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s command means His punishment.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إذا جاء أمرنا ﴾ عذابنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gushing oven is a metaphor for the crisis becoming severe and difficult.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وفار التنور ﴾ هو كناية عن اشتداد الأمر وصعوبته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says water surged from the bread oven, which was a stone belonging to Eve, and came to Noah.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه جاش الماء من تنور الخبز وكان من حجر لحواء فصار إلى نوح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further explanation identifies the oven with the face of the earth.
rows.anchor: وقيل التنور وجه الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to carry the people in the ship; the two of every kind are explained in Sūrat al-Muʾminūn.
rows.anchor: ﴿ من كل زوجين اثنين ﴾ تفسيره فى سورة ا 4 لمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah must carry his family and the believers, excluding any family member already destined for Hell; that prior decree follows God’s knowledge and willing of their chosen disbelief.
rows.anchor: واستثنى من أهله من سبق عليه القول أنه من أهل النار وما سبق عليه القول بذلك إلا للعلم بأنه يختار الكفر

rows.speaker: عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says eight were aboard: Noah, his family, his three sons, and their wives.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام كانوا ثمانية نوح وأهله وبنوه الثلاثة ونساؤهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report says there were ten people, five men and five women.
rows.anchor: وقيل كانوا عشرة خمسة رجال وخمس نسوة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report counts seventy-two men and women plus Noah’s three sons and their wives, seventy-eight total, evenly divided by sex.
rows.anchor: وقيل كانوا اثنين وسبعين رجالا ونساء وأولاد نوح سام وحام ويافث ونساؤهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala can attach to the command to board as a circumstantial phrase: they board while naming God or say it when the ship starts and comes to rest.
rows.anchor: بسم الله متصل باركوا حالا من الواو أى اركبوا فيها مسمين الله أو قائلين بسم الله وقت إجرائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time expressions may be nouns of time, or verbal nouns with an omitted genitive referring to the time of starting and mooring.
rows.anchor: اما لأن المجرى والمرسى للوقت واما لانهما مصدران كالاجراء والارساء حذف منهما الوقت المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the basmala clause stands independently as subject and predicate, explaining that the ship’s movement and anchoring occur through God’s name; Noah said it at each moment.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بسم الله مجراها ومرساها جملة برأسها غير متعلقة بما قبلها وهى مبتدأ وخبر

rows.speaker: حمزة وعلى وحفص
rows.claim: Hamzah, ʿAlī, and Ḥafṣ read the word for its course with fatḥa on mīm and kasra on rāʾ; Abū ʿAmr has kasra on rāʾ with mīm ḍamma, and the rest have both letters ḍamma.
rows.anchor: مجريها بفتح الميم وكسر الراء من جرى اما مصدر أو وقت حمزة وعلى وحفص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is forgiving to the believers aboard and merciful in delivering them.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إن ربي لغفور ﴾ لمن امن منهم ﴿ رحيم ﴾ حيث خلصهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs followed Pharaoh’s command, which exposes their ignorance: they followed manifest misguidance despite seeing the signs and knowing Moses had truth and guidance.
rows.anchor: أى الملأ ﴿ أمر فرعون وما أمر فرعون برشيد ﴾ هو تجهيل لمتبعيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh claimed divinity despite being human and practicing satanic injustice and evil; alternatively, his command was not good or praiseworthy in outcome.
rows.anchor: أنه ادعى الألوهية وهو بشر مثلهم وجاهز بالظلم والشر الذي لا يأتي إلا من شيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh goes ahead of his people on Judgment Day, with them following in his tracks; the wording explains how his command could not be right-guidance.
rows.anchor: أى يتقدمهم وهم على عقبه تفسيرا له وإيضاحا اى كيف يرشد أمر من هذه عاقبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rushd denotes anything praised and approved, while ghayy denotes anything blameworthy; qadama can mean to go ahead of someone.
rows.anchor: والرشد يستعمل فى كل ما يحمد ويرتضى كما استعمل الغى فى كل ما يذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The perfect tense presents Pharaoh’s leading his people into Hell as certain; as he led them into error, he leads them to the Fire and they follow.
rows.anchor: وجئ بلفظ الماضى لأن الماضى يدل على أمر موجود مقطوع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording likens Pharaoh to the one who reaches water first and his followers to those arriving after; Hell is the worst destination because fire is the opposite of thirst-quenching water.
rows.anchor: وشبه اتباعه بالواردة ثم قال وبئس الورد المورود الذى يردونه النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing in the heavens or earth is hidden from God, including people’s deeds.
rows.anchor: لا تخفى عليه خافية مما يجرى فيها فلا تخفى عليه أعمالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone’s affairs return to God, who will take vengeance for the Prophet against his opponents.
rows.anchor: أن يرجع إليه امرهم وأمرك فينتقم لك منهم

rows.speaker: نافع وحفص
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ read the verb as active, He returns, while the other reading presents affairs as being returned to Him.
rows.anchor: يرجع نافع وحفص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship God and rely on Him because He is sufficient as protector and guarantor.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فاعبده وتوكل عليه ﴾ فإنه كافيك وكافلك

rows.speaker: مدني وشامي وحفص
rows.claim: Madanī, Shāmī, and Ḥafṣ read the closing verb with tāʾ, addressing both the listener and others by predominance of the addressee.
rows.anchor: وبالتاء مدنى وشامى وحفص أى أنت وهم على تغليب المخاطب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported view says this verse is the Torah’s conclusion.
rows.anchor: قيل خاتمة التوراة هذه الآية

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A hadith says whoever wants to be the strongest of people should rely on God.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث من احب أن يكون أقوى الناس فليتوكل على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in lahu refers to whoever speaks openly, secretly, or privately.
rows.anchor: والضمير في ﴿ له ﴾ مردود على من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The protectors are groups of angels taking turns; the form may derive from assimilating the tāʾ of muʿtaqibāt into qāf, or from following on someone’s heels, because angels succeed one another or follow and record speech.
rows.anchor: جماعات من الملائكة تعتقب في حفظه والأصل معتقبات فأدغمت التاء في القاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels are positioned in front of and behind the person.
rows.anchor: أي قدامه ووراءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may describe angels appointed by God or mean that they protect by God’s command; alternatively they protect from His punishment through their prayers when someone sins.
rows.anchor: هما صفتان جميعا وليس من أمر الله بصلة للحفظ كأنه قيل له معقبات من أمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God changes a people’s wellbeing and blessing only when they change their good inward state through numerous sins.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم ﴾ من العافية والنعمة ﴿ حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم ﴾ من الحال الجميلة بكثرة المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God intends punishment for a people, nothing can repel it.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فلا مرد له ﴾ فلا يدفعه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have no protector besides God to manage their affairs and ward off punishment.
rows.anchor: من دون الله ممن يلى أمرهم ويدفع عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent Muhammad in a sending like the one just described, marked by distinction and merit over other missions.
rows.anchor: مثل ذلك الارسال أرسلناك ارسالا له شأن وفضل على سائر الارسالات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was sent among the last community after many earlier peoples and is the Seal of the Prophets.
rows.anchor: أرسلناك في أمة قد تقدمتها أمم كثيرة فهى آخر الأمم وأنت خاتم الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His task is to recite to them the mighty Scripture revealed to him.
rows.anchor: لتقرأ عليهم الكتاب العظيم الذي أوحينا اليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Raḥmān means the One whose mercy is vast enough to encompass everything.
rows.anchor: بالبليغ الرحمة الذي وسعت رحمته كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is Lord of everything and uniquely exalted above partners; Muhammad relies on Him for victory, returns to Him, and will be rewarded for persevering against them.
rows.anchor: اي هو ربى الواحد المتعالى عن الشركاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was sent with the nine signs.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ولقد أرسلنا موسى بآياتنا ﴾ التسع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to bring his people out can be read as an infinitive introduced by an, or as a direct command, since sending carries the sense of saying.
rows.anchor: بأن أخرج أو أي أخرج لأن الارسال فيه معنى القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The days of God are warnings about punitive events that befell Noah’s people, ʿĀd, and Thamūd, and by extension Arab battle days and wars.
rows.anchor: وأنذرهم بوقائعه التي وقعت على الأمم قبلهم قوم نوح وعاد وثمود ومنه ايام العرب لحروبها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the days of God days of blessing: cloud shade, manna and quail, and the sea split for the Israelites.
rows.anchor: أو بأيام الانعام حيث ظلل عليهم الغمام وأنزل عليهم المن والسلوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣabbār means patient through trials, and shakūr means grateful for gifts.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إن في ذلك لآيات لكل صبار ﴾ على البلايا ﴿ شكور ﴾ على العطايا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith is as if divided into two halves: patience and gratitude.
rows.anchor: كانه قال لكل مؤمن اذ الايمان نصفان نصف صبر ونصف شكر

rows.speaker: بصرى ومكى وشامى
rows.claim: Baṣran, Meccan, and Syrian readers pronounce the lām in al-mukhlaṣīn with kasra.
rows.anchor: وبكسر اللام بصرى ومكى وشامى استثنى المخلصين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan exempts the sincere because he knows his scheme cannot work on them and they will not accept it.
rows.anchor: استثنى المخلصين لأنه علم أن كيده لا يعمل فيهم ولا يقبلونه منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s declaration that this is a straight path means a true way that He undertakes to observe: Satan has no authority over God’s servants except those choosing to follow him in error.
rows.anchor: أي هذا طريق حق على أن أراعيه وهو أن لا يكون لك سلطان على عبادى إلا من اختار اتباعك

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb’s reading takes ʿalā as ilā, indicating the height of nobility and merit.
rows.anchor: وقيل معنى على إلى على يعقوب من علو الشرف والفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only those who freely follow Satan among the misguided fall under his authority.
rows.anchor: إلا من اختار اتباعك منهم لغوايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel lifted the towns of Lot’s people to heaven and then overturned them; the pronoun refers to those towns.
rows.anchor: رفعها جبريل عليه السلام إلى السماء ثم قلبها والضمير لقرى قوم لوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stones of sijjīl were rained upon them.
rows.anchor: وأمطرنا عليهم حجارة من سجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The perceptive are contemplative observers who seem to recognize what is hidden from an outward mark.
rows.anchor: للمتفرسين المتأملين كأنهم يعرفون باطن الشيء بسمة ظاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for the straight path is generic, and qasd is an active participle meaning straight: the path aims directly at its destination without deviation.
rows.anchor: المراد به الجنس ولذا قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guiding to the path that leads to truth belongs to God, as in the statement that guidance is upon Us; this is gracious favor, not an obligation on God.
rows.anchor: وليس ذلك للوجوب إذ لا يجب على الله شيء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation takes ʿalā as meaning ilā, toward God.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه وإلى الله

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains that God clarifies the evident straight path and invites people to it through proofs; crooked paths veer from straightness.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج معناه وعلى الله تبيين الطريق الواضح المستقيم والدعاء إليه بالحجج ومنها جائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God had willed, He would have given everyone the general guidance of gracious aid and favor.
rows.anchor: أراد هداية اللطف بالتوفيق والانعام به الهدى العام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are landmarks of roads, including mountains and anything else travelers use for orientation.
rows.anchor: هي معالم الطرق وكل ما يستدل به السابلة من جبل وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The star may mean stars generally or specifically the Pleiades, the two Furqadān, Banāt Naʿsh, and al-Jady.
rows.anchor: المراد بالنجم الجنس أو هو التريا والفرقدان وبنات نعش والجدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting the star and inserting they emphasizes exclusive guidance; the referent is Quraysh, singled out because they navigate by stars and have exceptional knowledge, making gratitude and reflection especially incumbent.
rows.anchor: كأنه قيل وبالنجم خصوصا هؤلاء خصوصا يهتدون فمن المراد بهم قلت كانه أراد قريشا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dīn means obedience, and wāṣiban means obligatory and constant because every blessing comes from God, so obedience is due from each recipient.
rows.anchor: واجبا ثابتا لأن كل نعمة منه فالطاعة واجبة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, wāṣiban means that reward and punishment are permanent.
rows.anchor: أو وله الجزاء دائما يعنى الثواب والعقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse challenges people about fearing anyone besides God.
rows.anchor: أفغير الله تتقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative to bees is feminine because nahl is a feminine noun on the pattern of nakhl/nakhlah; an is explanatory since revelation here carries the sense of speech.
rows.anchor: هي أن المفسرة لأن الايحاء فيه معنى القول قال الزجاج واحد النحل نحلة كنحل ونخلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition min indicates some mountains, trees, or human-built structures, since bees do not build in every such place; yʿarishūn refers to people raising roofs or making hives.
rows.anchor: يرفعون من سقوف البيت أو ما يبنون للنحل في الجبال والشجر والبيوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in yʿarishūn refers to people.
rows.anchor: والضمير في يعرشون للناس

rows.speaker: شامي وأبو بكر
rows.claim: Shāmī and Abū Bakr read the rāʾ of yʿarishūn with ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وبضم الراء شامى وأبو بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After building their homes, bees eat whatever fruit they desire.
rows.anchor: أي ابنى البيوت ثم كلى كل ثمرة تشتهيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commanded paths may be the routes God inspires bees to follow in making honey, or their easy return routes from distant feeding grounds without getting lost.
rows.anchor: فادخلى الطرق التي ألهمك وأفهمك في عمل العسل أو إذا أكلت الثمار في المواضع البعيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word dhululan may describe the pathways, which God made easy, or the bee, which is submissive and unresisting in obedience.
rows.anchor: جمع ذلول وهي حال من السبل لأن الله تعالى ذللها وسهلها أو من الضمير في فاسلكى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The drink issuing from the bees is honey, which they emit from their mouths.
rows.anchor: يريد العسل لأنه مما يشرب تلقيه من فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Honey’s white, yellow, and red colors may reflect the bee’s age or the colors of its foods.
rows.anchor: منه أبيض وأصفر وأحمر من الشباب والكهول والشيب أو على الوان أغذيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Honey is one of the beneficial medicines and is cited by physicians as an ingredient in remedies; the verse does not claim it cures every patient.
rows.anchor: لأنه من جملة الأدوية النافعة وقل معجون من المعاجين لم يذكر الأطباء فيه العسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite word healing either magnifies the healing in honey or limits it to some healing, since an indefinite noun in an affirmative clause is specific.
rows.anchor: وتنكيره لتعظيم الشفاء الذي فيه أو لأن فيه بعض الشفاء

rows.speaker: عليه السلام
rows.claim: A man complained that his brother had severe diarrhea; after honey was prescribed twice and the complaint worsened, the speaker said God tells the truth and the brother’s belly lies, and the man recovered after giving honey again.
rows.anchor: شكا رجل استطلاق بطن أخيه فقال عليه السلام اسقه عسلا فجاءه وقال زاده شرا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says honey heals every illness and the Qur’an heals what is in hearts, so people should use both cures.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه العسل شفاء من كل داء والقرآن شفاء لما في الصدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nasafī calls it an innovation of the Rāfiḍa to interpret the bees as ʿAlī and his followers.
rows.anchor: ومن بدع الروافض أن المراد بالنحل على وقومه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An anecdote mocks the claim that bees signify Banū Hāshim and their knowledge: a man jokes that one should eat and drink what comes from their bellies, making al-Mahdī laugh and the story an object of ridicule for al-Manṣūr.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم أن رجلا قال عند المهدى إنما النحل بنو هاشم يخرج من بطونهم العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflecting on the bee’s astonishing behavior shows that God endowed it with knowledge and instinct, as He endowed rational people with reason.
rows.anchor: في عجب أمرها فيعلمون أن الله أودعها علما بذلك وفطنها كما أعطى أولى العقول عقولهم

rows.speaker: روى أنه
rows.claim: A report says Abraham always ate with a guest; when none appeared, he delayed eating until angels came as humans, feigned leprosy, and were invited, so he could thank God for his health while accepting their trial.
rows.anchor: روى أنه كان لا يتغدى إلا مع ضيف فلم يجد ذات يوم ضيفا فاخر غداءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God selected and chose Abraham for prophethood.
rows.anchor: ﴿ اجتباه ﴾ اختصه واصطفاه للنبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guided Abraham to the religion of Islam.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وهداه إلى صراط مستقيم ﴾ إلى ملة الاسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Raḥmān is nominative as praise, meaning He is the Merciful; ʿalā al-ʿarsh is the predicate of an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: رفع على المدح أي هو الرحمن

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj interprets istawā as istawlā, exercising dominion.
rows.anchor: ﴿ استوى ﴾ استولى عن الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the throne, the greatest creation, signals the rest; alternatively, sitting on a throne conventionally signifies kingship, as an extended hand signifies generosity without implying a literal hand.
rows.anchor: ونبه بذكر العرش وهو أعظم المخلوقات على غيره وقيل لما كان الاستواء على العرش

rows.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: A saying attributed to ʿAlī holds that istiwāʾ is known, its modality inconceivable, belief obligatory, and questioning about it an innovation.
rows.anchor: المذهب قول علي رضي الله عنه الاستواء غير مجهول والتكييف غير معقول والإيمان به واجب

rows.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: The same saying states that God existed without place and remains as He was before creating place, unchanged.
rows.anchor: لأنه تعالى كان ولا مكان فهو على ما كان قبل خلق المكان لم يتغير عما كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is one in His essence even though descriptions of His attributes use different expressions, refuting the claim that invoking His names invokes multiple gods.
rows.anchor: أي هو واحد بذاته وان افترقت عبارات صفاته رد لقولهم أنك تدعو آلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥusnā is the feminine form of al-iḥsān.
rows.anchor: والحسنى تأنيث الاحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh addresses both Moses and Aaron, then singles out Moses because he is the principal prophet while Aaron follows him.
rows.anchor: خاطبهما ثم بادي احدهما لأن موسى هو الأصل في النبوة وهرون نابعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If khalqahu is the first object of aʿṭā, God gave each thing its constitution and everything needed for its use; if it is the second object, He gave each thing a form suited to its function, such as the eye for sight and ear for hearing.
rows.anchor: أول مفعولي أعطي أي أعطى حليقته كل شيء يحتاجون إليه ويرتفقون به أو ثانيهما أي أعطي كل شيء صورته وشكله

rows.speaker: نصير
rows.claim: Naṣīr reads khalqahu adjectivally with either the annexed noun or its complement, meaning God gave every created thing a provision.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نصير خلقه صفة للمضاف أو للمضاف إليه أي أعطي كل شيء مخلوق عطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then God guided each creature, directing it to what it needs.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ثم هدى ﴾ عرف فكيف يرتمق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s guidance directs creatures toward livelihood in this world and happiness in the next.
rows.anchor: بما أعطى للمعيشة في الدنيا والسعادة في العقبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh asks about the condition of past peoples and vanished generations, including the fates of those who were wretched and those who prospered.
rows.anchor: فما حال الأمم الخالية والرمم البالية سأله عن حال من تقدم من القرون وعن شقاء من شقي منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses answers that knowledge of past generations is with God, recorded in the Preserved Tablet; this is unseen knowledge reserved to Him, and Moses knows only what God reveals.
rows.anchor: هذا سؤال عن الغيب وقد استاثر الله به لا يعلمه إلا هو وما أنا إلا عبد مثلك لا أعلم منه إلا ما أخبرني به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā yaḍillu means God does not miss or err, including in determining people’s felicity or misery.
rows.anchor: أي لا يخطئ في سعادة الناس وشقاوتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā yansā means He does not forget their reward or punishment; alternatively, the record preserves what He knows so the angels can see creatures’ actions accord with His knowledge.
rows.anchor: ثوابهم وعقابهم وقيل لا ينسى ما علم فيذكره الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun alladhī may modify Rabbī, serve as the predicate of an omitted subject, or be accusative as praise.
rows.anchor: مرفوع صفة لربي أو خبر مبتدأ محذوف أو منصوب على المدح

rows.speaker: كوفي
rows.claim: Kufans read mahdan, while the other readers have mihādan; both are words for a spread-out, prepared surface.
rows.anchor: كوفي وغيرهم مهادا وهما لغتان لما يبسط ويفرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth was made a resting place, paths were made through it, the water is rain, and salk means made.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وسلك ﴾ أي جعل ﴿ لكم فيها سبلا ﴾ طرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift in fa-akhrajnā from third person to first-person plural is stylistic; alternatively, God begins speaking after Moses, or Moses says we produced the plants through farming and planting.
rows.anchor: نقل الكلام من الغيبة إلى لفظ المتكلم المطاع للإفتنان وقيل ثم كلام موسى ثم اخبر الله تعالى عن نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azwāj are kinds, nabāt is a verbal noun used for plant in singular and plural, and shattā describes diverse kinds or plants differing in use, color, scent, and shape for people and animals.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أزواجا ﴾ أصنافا ﴿ من نبات ﴾ هو مصدر سمى به النبات فاستوى فيه الواحد والجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A blessing is that livestock feed on vegetation left over because people cannot eat it.
rows.anchor: ومن نعمة الله تعالى أن أرزاقنا تحصل بعمل الانعام وقد جعل الله علفها مما يفضل عن حاجتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permission to eat and pasture animals is a circumstantial clause attached to God’s bringing forth plants: He produced kinds of vegetation while allowing some to be eaten and some used as fodder.
rows.anchor: حال من الضمير في فأخرجنا والمعنى أخرجنا اصناف النبات آذنين في الانتفاع بها مبيحين أن تأكلوا بعضها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The things mentioned are signs, meaning indications.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إن في ذلك ﴾ في الذي ذكرت ﴿ لآيات ﴾ لدلالات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ulū al-nuhā are people of reason; nuhya is singular because reason restrains from forbidden acts or serves as the endpoint consulted in affairs.
rows.anchor: لذوي العقول واحدها نهية تنهى عن المحظور أو ينتهى اليها في الامور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage recalls God’s favor to Israel after He rescued them from the sea and destroyed Pharaoh and his people.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر منته على بني إسرائيل بعدما أنجاهم من البحر وأهلك فرعون وقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to Israel reflects God’s order to Moses to travel by night with His servants and His words to the Israelites.
rows.anchor: أي أوحينا إلى موسى أن أسر بعبادي وقلنا يا بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their enemy is Pharaoh, and the appointment at the right side of the Mount was for the giving of scripture; God promised Moses this place and that he select seventy men to witness the Torah’s revelation.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن الله عز وجل وعد موسى أن يأتي هذا لمكان ويختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise is attributed to Israel because it was made to their prophet and leaders and its benefits and law returned to them; al-ayman is accusative as an adjective of side.
rows.anchor: وإنما نسب اليهم المواعدة لأنها كانت لنبيهم ونقبائهم واليهم رجعت منافعها التي قام بها شرعهم ودينهم والأيمن نصب لأنه صفة جانب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading puts al-ayman in the genitive by attraction to the preceding word.
rows.anchor: وقرئ بالجر على الجوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manna and quail were sent down to Israel in the wilderness.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ونزلنا عليكم المن والسلوى ﴾ في التيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭayyibāt means lawful foods.
rows.anchor: ﴿ كلوا من طيبات ﴾ حلالات

rows.speaker: كوفي غير عاصم
rows.claim: Kufan readers except ʿĀṣim read the singular forms for God’s saving, promise, and provision in the preceding address.
rows.anchor: أنجيتكم وواعدتك ورزقتكم كوفي غير عاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Transgressing the provision means violating God’s limits by ingratitude and spending it in sins, or wronging one another.
rows.anchor: ولا تتعدوا حدود الله فيه بأن تكفروا النعم وتنفقوها في المعاصي أولا يظلم بعضكم بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s wrath is His punishment; whoever incurs it has perished or fallen.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فيحل عليكم غضبي ﴾ عقوبتي ﴿ ومن يحلل عليه غضبي فقد هوى ﴾ هلك أو سقط سقوطا لا نهوض

rows.speaker: على والباقون
rows.claim: ʿAlī reads the two verbs with fatḥa; the others read both with kasra, where the kasra means becoming due and the ḍamma means descending.
rows.anchor: قرا على فيحل ويحلل والباون بكسرهما فالمسكور في معنى الوجوب
